# FG-WEB-0008

| 項目 | 値 |
|---|---|
| HTTP ステータス | 503 |
| 重大度 | warn |
| Runbook | [`connections`](../../ops/runbooks/connections.md) |
| 発生させるテスト | `connections_over_the_per_peer_cap_get_503` |

## 利用者向けメッセージ

- ja: サーバーが混み合っています。しばらくしてから再度お試しください。
- en: The server is busy. Try again later.
- id: Server sedang sibuk. Coba lagi nanti.

## 原因 (cause)

A new connection was refused before any request was read, because the server already holds `server.max_connections` open connections, or `server.max_connections_per_peer` from the same socket peer address. The client gets this 503 with `Retry-After` and the connection is closed. A list request (`GET /api/v1/projects` / `/groups`) is refused the same way (503 with `Retry-After: 1`, the connection stays open) when `api.list_max_concurrent` list scans already run, or `api.list_max_concurrent_per_principal` for the same user.

## 調べ方 (diagnosis)

The log event carries `reason` (`connection_limit`: the whole server is full; `peer_limit`: one peer holds its share), `peer` (the socket peer IP; behind a reverse proxy this is the proxy; an IPv6 peer is counted by its /64 prefix, so all addresses of one /64 share the cap, while `peer` in the log is the actual address of the refused connection), `reason=summary` (a line written after the flood stopped or at shutdown: only `suppressed`, the refusals not logged one by one), `limit`, `open` (connections held right now) and `suppressed` (refusals since the previous log line: at most one line per second is written). A refusal is logged once, at the accept loop, with a connection-level request_id (also in the response body). Many `peer_limit` refusals for one `peer`: a client or script opens too many connections, or connections are held open (slow readers are closed by `server.write_idle_timeout_ms`, idle keep-alive by `server.header_read_timeout_ms`, old ones by `server.keep_alive_max_ms`); when `peer` is the reverse proxy, the cap counts all its clients together and is too low for the proxy. `connection_limit` while no peer dominates: real load, or many slow clients. `operation=response_write` on FG-WEB-0002 is the related event for a client that stopped reading. `reason=list_concurrency` (from a list route, with `scope=global|principal` and `max`; request_id of the refused request; logged once per refusal): every list request scans up to 1001 rows whatever `limit` is, so the number running at once is capped. `scope=principal`: one user (script, UI polling) keeps more than `api.list_max_concurrent_per_principal` (default 2) lists running — find the user in the same request_id's events; `scope=global`: `api.list_max_concurrent` (default 16) are running, which usually means the scans are slow — look for `FG-WEB-0002 operation=project_page|group_page` (a slow database or very many projects / groups) before raising the cap.

## 対処 (fix)

Find the peer holding connections (runbook connections); stop the misbehaving client, or raise `server.max_connections_per_peer` / `server.max_connections` (keep per-peer at most the total) and restart. For a reverse proxy raise the per-peer cap to the proxy's expected concurrency. For `reason=list_concurrency` fix the slow scan or the polling client first (runbook connections); raise `api.list_max_concurrent` / `api.list_max_concurrent_per_principal` (per-user at most the total) only when the database has room, and restart.
